topic: Compound Interest — Formulae and Applications (W11 B2)

questions.stem: Find the compound interest on Rs. 10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Amount = P(1 + r/100)^n = 10000×(1.1)² = 10000×1.21 = 12,100. CI = A - P = 12,100 - 10,000 = Rs. 2,100. Short trick: For 2 years at r%, CI = SI + (r% of SI for 1 year) = 2000 + 10% of 1000 = 2000 + 100 = 2100. SI for 2 years = 10000×10×2/100 = 2000. Trap: 2,000 = SI answer (wrong — CI is always more than SI for same terms).

questions.stem: A sum of Rs. 8,000 amounts to Rs. 9,261 in 3 years at compound interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
The difference between CI and SI on Rs. 5,000 for 2 years at 8% per annum is:
questions.explanation: C is correct. Formula: CI - SI = P×(r/100)² for 2 years. = 5000×(8/100)² = 5000×0.0064 = 32. Verify: SI = 5000×8×2/100 = 800. CI: Year 1 interest = 400; Year 2 interest = 400 + 8% of 400 = 400+32=432; Total CI = 832. Difference = 832-800 = 32 ✓. Short trick: Difference = P × (r/100)² = 5000 × (0.08)² = 5000 × 0.0064 = 32.

questions.stem: At what rate of compound interest per annum will Rs. 1,200 become Rs. 1,348.32 in 2 years?
What is the compound interest on Rs. 16,000 at 20% per annum for 9 months, compounded quarterly?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Quarterly rate = 20/4 = 5% per quarter. 9 months = 3 quarters (n=3). A = 16000×(1.05)³ = 16000×1.157625 = 18,522. CI = 18,522 - 16,000 = 2,522. Compute: 1.05³ = 1.157625; 16000×1.157625 = 18522. Trap: 2,420 = using annual rate for 9 months as simple SI; 2,424.80 = uses half-year compounding instead of quarterly.

questions.stem: In how many years will Rs. 3,000 become Rs. 3,993 at 10% compound interest per annum?
A certain sum doubles itself in 5 years under compound interest. In how many years will it become 8 times itself?
questions.explanation: C is correct. If P doubles in 5 years: (1+r/100)^5 = 2. To become 8 times: (1+r/100)^n = 8 = 2³ = [(1+r/100)^5]³. So (1+r/100)^n = (1+r/100)^15 → n = 15 years. Shortcut: 2→5 years; 4=2²→10 years; 8=2³→15 years. Each doubling takes 5 years; 8 = 3 doublings → 3×5 = 15 years. Trap: 10 years = only 2 doublings (gives 4 times, not 8); 20 = 4 doublings (gives 16 times).

A bank offers 12% interest compounded half-yearly. What is the effective annual rate?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Half-yearly rate = 12/2 = 6% per half-year. Effective annual rate = (1.06)² - 1 = 1.1236 - 1 = 0.1236 = 12.36%. Verify: Rs. 100 grows to 100×1.06=106 after 6 months, then 106×1.06=112.36 after 1 year. Effective rate = 12.36%. Trap: 12% = the nominal rate (ignores compounding effect); 14.4% = 12%×1.2 (wrong multiplication).
